configPages.name: Policies
configPages.navPathSourceQuote: From the Invoice Processing Admin menu, select Policies.
navPathAlternates: Administration > Invoice > Policies > Auto Submit Conditions

configPages.name: Group Configurations
configPages.navPathSourceQuote: 2.  On the Administration > Invoice > Group Configurations page in the Policies column, click Modify for the group you want to modify.
navPathAlternates: Administration > Invoice > Group Configurations > Vendor Access
Administration > Invoice > Invoice Processing Admin > Group Configurations

configPages.name: Invoice Settings
configPages.navPathSourceQuote: From the Invoice Processing Admin menu, select Invoice Settings.

configFields.name: Policy Name
configFields.label: Policy Name
configFields.sourceQuote: Displays the name of the policy
configFields.notes: Column on the Policies list page (read-only display). The editable counterpart is the Name field on the New Policy / Modify Policy General page.

configFields.name: Editable By
configFields.label: Editable By
configFields.sourceQuote: Displays the group rights that an administrator must have to modify a policy
configFields.notes: Read-only column on the Policies list page; reflects the Editable By Group(s) value set on the policy. A second topic notes: 'Although the Editable by Group(s) column appears on the Policies List page, the administrator uses the Groups tool to assign the policy to a group.'

configFields.name: Applies to
configFields.label: Applies to
configFields.sourceQuote: Displays the groups for which this policy currently applies, including all groups that are below it in the hierarchical structure
configFields.notes: Read-only column on the Policies list page. The same file warns that the actual policy-to-group assignment happens in Group Configurations, not here.

configFields.name: Copy Policy
configFields.label: Copy Policy
configFields.sourceQuote: Select Copy Policy.
configFields.notes: The documented way to create a policy: select an existing policy, then Copy Policy; the New Policy page appears. Corroborated in policy-c8ec906b.md: 'Select the Payment Request Policy, then click Copy Policy and rename the copied policy'.

configFields.name: Modify
configFields.label: Modify
configFields.sourceQuote: Choose Modify.
configFields.notes: Opens the Modify Policy page (General tab) for the selected policy. Corroborated: 'On the Policies page, select a policy and then click Modify to open the Modify Policy page.' (assign-to-a-policy-a12befe1.md)

configFields.name: Remove
configFields.label: Remove
configFields.sourceQuote: Select Remove.
configFields.notes: Deletes the selected policy. Caution in the same file: forms assigned to a deleted policy are retained in the database and cannot be deleted.

configFields.name: Expense Types
configFields.label: Expense Types
configFields.sourceQuote: This is done by using the Expense Types button after selecting the policy:
configFields.notes: Policies-page button; opens the Modify Policy page listing the policy's expense types with Activate / Deactivate.

configFields.name: Print Format
configFields.label: Print Format
configFields.sourceQuote: To do this, use the Print Format button after selecting the policy.
configFields.notes: Policies-page button; opens the Modify Policy page where a print format is activated/deactivated for the policy.

configFields.name: Auto Submit Conditions
configFields.label: Auto Submit Conditions
configFields.sourceQuote: Select Auto Submit Conditions, and then select Insert.
configFields.notes: Policies-page button opening the auto-submit condition editor for the selected policy. Also reachable as a wizard step: 'The Auto Submit Conditions step appears.' (create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md)

configFields.name: Insert
configFields.label: Insert
configFields.sourceQuote: Create the condition(s) for the submit action in the condition editor, selecting Insert for each new condition as needed.
configFields.notes: Adds a new row to the auto-submit condition editor. The corpus does not enumerate the operators or operands available in the editor.

configFields.name: Name
configFields.label: Name
configFields.sourceQuote: Enter a name for the new policy.
configFields.notes: New Policy / Modify Policy General page. Free-text policy name.

configFields.name: Header Form
configFields.label: Header Form
configFields.sourceQuote: Select the Payment Request Header Form to be associated with the new policy. The default information that appears in this field is from the copied policy.
configFields.notes: Options come from Payment Request Header Forms built in the Form Types area of the Administrator; the corpus does not enumerate them.

configFields.name: Line Item Form
configFields.label: Line Item Form
configFields.sourceQuote: Select the Line Item Form to be associated with the new policy. The default information that appears in this field is from the copied policy.
configFields.notes: Options are Line Item Forms created in the Form Types area of the Administrator; not enumerated in the corpus.

configFields.name: Allocation Form
configFields.label: Allocation Form
configFields.sourceQuote: Select the Allocation Form to be associated with the new policy. The default information that appears in this field is from the copied policy.
configFields.notes: Designating an allocation form is what activates the allocation feature: 'If the allocation feature is not activated (by designating an allocation form), the separator is not used.' (components-of-the-policy-3bf075f8.md)

configFields.name: Vendor Form
configFields.label: Vendor Form
configFields.sourceQuote: Select the Vendor Address Form to be associated with the new policy. The default information that appears in this field is from the copied policy.
configFields.notes: Field label is 'Vendor Form'; the description calls the object a Vendor Address Form. Options built in Form Types; not enumerated.

configFields.name: Can request a new vendor?
configFields.label: Can request a new vendor?
configFields.sourceQuote: Select Yes to allow an employee to request a new vendor be added to the master vendor list. Selecting Yes displays a Request New Vendor link on the Create Payment Request Header page.
configFields.notes: A Yes-valued selector, not a check box — the corpus says 'Select Yes', distinguishing it from the neighbouring 'Select this check box' controls. Only 'Yes' is ever written; the complementary option is never named in 2026_08, so it is deliberately omitted rather than guessed. Downstream effect is enumerated: selecting Yes reveals a Request New Vendor link on the Create Payment Request Header page.

configFields.name: Can Invoice Users Assign Requests:
configFields.label: Can Invoice Users Assign Requests:
configFields.sourceQuote: Select this check box if you want to allow the Invoice User to have privileges to re-assign an invoice they have unassigned from themselves.
configFields.notes: Label carries a trailing colon in the corpus table. Explicitly a check box.

configFields.name: Is PO Policy?
configFields.label: Is PO Policy?
configFields.sourceQuote: Select this check box to make this a purchase order (PO) enabled policy - doing this:
configFields.notes: Master toggle for the PO policy type. Selecting it reveals the PO Configuration options. Written as 'Is PO Policy' (no question mark) in purchase-order-policy-fields-4aa0ac1b.md and policy-c8ec906b.md. Cannot be cleared once invoices exist: 'the PO policy cannot be changed to a non-PO policy unless there are no invoices associated with the PO policy.'

configFields.name: PO Header Form
configFields.label: PO Header Form
configFields.sourceQuote: -   PO Header Form
configFields.notes: Revealed only when the policy is a PO policy. Same behaviour as the standard Header Form: 'PO form types act just as standard forms'. Options not enumerated.

configFields.name: PO Line Item Form
configFields.label: PO Line Item Form
configFields.sourceQuote: -   PO Line Item Form
configFields.notes: Revealed only when the policy is a PO policy. Options not enumerated in the corpus.

configFields.name: PO Allocation Form
configFields.label: PO Allocation Form
configFields.sourceQuote: -   PO Allocation Form
configFields.notes: Revealed only when the policy is a PO policy. Options not enumerated in the corpus.

configFields.name: Enable Concur Receiving
configFields.label: Enable Concur Receiving
configFields.sourceQuote: In the PO Configuration section of the page that appears, select the Enable Concur Receiving option.
configFields.notes: Activates manual quantity-receipt entry and three-way matching. Located in the PO Configuration section of the policy page; the same file notes that once activated, the Purchase Order Receipt form in Forms and Fields is automatically used. Also listed among the PO Forms controls in create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md.

configFields.name: PO Matching Ruleset
configFields.label: PO Matching Ruleset
configFields.sourceQuote: PO Matching Ruleset: This is where you specify the matching rule set that will instruct the system how to react whenever a user-defined variance is detected between the matching invoice and PO.
configFields.notes: Appears only on PO policies: 'Adds the PO Matching Ruleset option where PO matching rules are specified' (create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md). Rule sets are per-policy: 'PO Matching Rule Sets (which include Receipt Confirmation outcomes) can differ per policy.' (match-rule-set-per-policy-8b14149d.md). Option list is tenant-built in Purchase Order Matching Rules and is not enumerated.

configFields.name: Is Purchase Request Policy
configFields.label: Is Purchase Request Policy
configFields.sourceQuote: Now the Is Purchase Request Policy check box is exposed and, when selected, displays the Purchase Request Configuration options (forms and workflow selections) as shown in the figure above.
configFields.notes: Second-level conditional control: exposed only after Is PO Policy is selected. Selecting it reveals a Purchase Request Configuration group of form and workflow selections, which the corpus does not break out field by field.

configFields.name: Invoice Workflow
configFields.label: Invoice Workflow
configFields.sourceQuote: Select an invoice workflow to be associated with the new policy. The default information that is displayed in the field is from the copied policy.
configFields.notes: Options are workflows built in the Workflows area of the Administrator; not enumerated. Note a workflow can be reused: 'A workflow can be assigned to multiple policies.' (implementation-guidelines-for-policies-0c35d480.md)

configFields.name: Scan Configuration
configFields.label: Scan Configuration
configFields.sourceQuote: Select a scan configuration to be associated with this policy. There is no default value assigned; if you do not select a configuration, the scan functionality will not be active for the policy.
configFields.notes: No default value; leaving it unset disables scan for the policy. Cardinality is documented: 'One configuration can be used by multiple policies; however, each policy can only use a single scan configuration.' (step-2-assign-the-scan-configuration-to-a-policy-634c76ba.md). Options come from the Scan Configurations page in Image Handling.

configFields.name: Imaging Configuration
configFields.label: Imaging Configuration
configFields.sourceQuote: Select an imaging configuration to be associated with this policy. There is no default value assigned; if you do not select a configuration, the imaging functionality will not be active for the policy.
configFields.notes: No default; unset means imaging is inactive for the policy. Setting it makes the View Image link appear on the Payment Request page for the Invoice Processor. Options are created in Image Handling (invoice) / Vendor Handling (vendor); not enumerated.

configFields.name: Timestamp Configuration
configFields.label: Timestamp Configuration
configFields.sourceQuote: Select Japan e-Bunsho from the Timestamp Configurationlist.
configFields.notes: Only one option value is ever named in the 2026_08 corpus, so validValues is that single value and may be incomplete — the corpus does not publish the full list. Quote reproduced verbatim including the missing space in 'Timestamp Configurationlist'. Field purpose: 'Timestamp Configuration applies to clients that use the Invoice e-Bunsho Timestamp feature to maintain legal compliance with eBunsho regulations regarding digital invoices.' (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md). Visible on modify: 'On the Administration >Invoice > Policies page, when Invoice Admins modify a policy, the admin will see the Timestamp Configuration field.' (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/invoice-admin-experience-840503f4.md).

configFields.name: Allocation Separator
configFields.label: Allocation Separator
configFields.sourceQuote: Select an appropriate allocation separator. This separator appears to the employee when selecting the allocations that separate the hierarchy (for example, 9543-4558-477).
configFields.notes: Default is documented but the option list is not: 'Allocation Separator: This symbol separates segments of the allocation code. The default is the hyphen (-).' (components-of-the-policy-3bf075f8.md). Unused if no allocation form is designated.

configFields.name: External ID
configFields.label: External ID
configFields.sourceQuote: Generated by the system but can be edited, this value is a unique identifier for the policy that is drawn on by the system when matching invoices and purchase orders to the policy and to one another as a result.
configFields.notes: System-generated but editable; must be unique. Corroborated in purchase-order-policy-fields-4aa0ac1b.md: 'External ID: This unique identifier lets the system associate the policy to all invoices and POs that include this same identifier.'

configFields.name: Editable By Group(s)
configFields.label: Editable By Group(s)
configFields.sourceQuote: If you select Global, then the information can be edited or deleted by any employee assigned to administer the Global group. Administrators assigned at lower levels in the hierarchy may copy the information but may not edit or delete it.
configFields.notes: 'Global' is the only system-defined value the corpus names; the remaining options are the customer's own group-hierarchy nodes and are therefore not enumerable as structural knowledge. Selection is constrained by the admin's own rights: 'Depending on your rights, you may not be able to select the Global group. This means you are only allowed to select your group or groups that fall below your group in the hierarchy.' Field description on the wizard: 'Select the group(s) for which an administrator must have administration rights to modify the policy.' (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md).

configFields.name: Bill To (Optional)
configFields.label: Bill To (Optional)
configFields.sourceQuote: Add a default Bill To address to associate with new invoices.
configFields.notes: CONFLICT in the corpus: labelled '(Optional)' in the Create a New Policy table, but for purchase-request policies policy-c8ec906b.md states 'Bill To is a required field and must be filled out to complete the policy configuration.' Addresses are maintained via Set a Default Shipping and Billing Address; the option list is tenant data.

configFields.name: Expense Type
configFields.label: Expense Type
configFields.sourceQuote: Displays the expense types defined for the policy.
configFields.notes: Column on the Expense Types for Policy step / Modify Policy expense-type list. 'Clicking the name of an expense type displays the Expense Type Properties page' (same file); elsewhere named the Modify Expense Type Properties window.

configFields.name: Policy Status
configFields.label: Policy Status
configFields.sourceQuote: Provides a status, either Active or Inactive, for each expense type. Active expense types are available from the Expense Type list when creating an invoice, while Inactive expense types are unavailable.
configFields.notes: Genuinely enumerated -- the only two-value enumeration on this page. Newly created expense types land here as Inactive: 'All new expense types appear in the Policies tool as Inactive.' (expense-types-and-policies-a01e2537.md)

configFields.name: Activate
configFields.label: Activate
configFields.sourceQuote: Select the desired expense types and click Activate or Deactivate to change the policy status.
configFields.notes: Acts on the current multi-selection: 'You can select individual expense types or use Shift+click or Ctrl+click to select multiple expense types.' (change-the-status-of-an-expense-type-cf452b6a.md). The same button pair also appears on the Print Format list: 'Select a policy, and then select either Activate or Deactivate.'

configFields.name: Deactivate
configFields.label: Deactivate
configFields.sourceQuote: Select the desired expense types and click Activate or Deactivate to change the policy status.
configFields.notes: Paired with Activate. Note a label typo in change-the-status-of-an-expense-type-cf452b6a.md, which writes 'Select Active or Deactivate.' -- a matcher should tolerate both Active and Activate.

configFields.name: Apply Auto Submit to Assignment
configFields.label: Apply Auto Submit to Assignment
configFields.sourceQuote: (Optional) Select Apply Auto Submit to Assignment if you would like the system to automatically attempt to submit an invoice on assignment.
configFields.notes: Check box inside the Auto Submit Conditions area. Without it, auto-submit fires on import only; with it, also on assignment of the invoice to an employee.

configFields.name: Enable Attendee
configFields.label: Enable Attendee
configFields.sourceQuote: Select this check box to enable the Attendee feature.
configFields.notes: Reachable from THIS page via the Expense Types button: 'The options in the Attendees step in the Expense Types tool in Invoice Administration are also available in the Policies tool.' and 'Double-click an expense type. The Modify Expense Type Properties window appears with the options that are also available in the Expense Types tool.' (same file). Setting is per policy AND per expense type.

configFields.name: Show Cost per Attendee
configFields.label: Show Cost per Attendee
configFields.sourceQuote: Select this check box to allow users to view the amount of the expense allotted to each attendee.
configFields.notes: Per-policy, per-expense-type option in the Modify Expense Type Properties window opened from the Policies page. Confirmed as a policy-scoped setting by settings-for-policy-and-expense-type-92703364.md.

configFields.name: Allow users to edit the Cost per Attendee
configFields.label: Allow users to edit the Cost per Attendee
configFields.sourceQuote: Select this check box to allow users to edit the amounts in the Amount column.
configFields.notes: Per-policy, per-expense-type option in the Modify Expense Type Properties window opened from the Policies page.

configFields.name: Allow users to enter the count of "No Shows"
configFields.label: Allow users to enter the count of "No Shows"
configFields.sourceQuote: Select this check box to allow users to account for "No Shows," that is attendees who were invited but did not attend.
configFields.notes: Per-policy, per-expense-type option in the Modify Expense Type Properties window opened from the Policies page. Casing of 'No Shows' varies between topics.

configFields.name: Allow users to edit the count of attendees
configFields.label: Allow users to edit the count of attendees
configFields.sourceQuote: Select this check box to allow users to enter a count (number of unnamed attendees) for this expense type.
configFields.notes: Per-policy, per-expense-type option in the Modify Expense Type Properties window opened from the Policies page. Used in conjunction with attendee type settings.

configFields.name: Include user as an attendee by default
configFields.label: Include user as an attendee by default
configFields.sourceQuote: If this check box is selected, Concur Invoice automatically adds the user as an attendee when the user accesses the attendees section the first time (when no attendees are assigned to the entry).
configFields.notes: Per-policy, per-expense-type option in the Modify Expense Type Properties window opened from the Policies page.

configFields.name: Display the Add New Attendees button from the attendee table
configFields.label: Display the Add New Attendees button from the attendee table
configFields.sourceQuote: If this check box is selected, Invoice adds the Add New Attendee button to the Attendee section of the Attendee tab.
configFields.notes: LABEL DRIFT -- the dedicated Policies-tool procedure names it without 'Add': 'Clear the Display the New Attendee button from the attendee table (shown in its selected, default state in the figure below).' (procedure-suppress-the-new-attendee-button-by-expense-type-9a8edae0.md, which reaches it via Administration > Invoice > Policies > select policy > Expense Types > double-click expense type). Default state is selected.

configFields.name: Group
configFields.label: Group
configFields.sourceQuote: Select the correct group as it should appear within the other tools and to the employee.
configFields.notes: First row of the "Table 1: Configuration for Group fields" table in the Add Groups topic. The value is chosen through a separate Select Group window opened by New, not typed. Available groups are constrained by the admin's rights: "You can only create group configurations for groups for which you are assigned rights and for groups below those groups." (same file).

configFields.name: Group Name
configFields.label: Group Name
configFields.sourceQuote: Type a unique name that describes this group. When creating other configurations, you will see the group name and not the group path, so make sure it is descriptive of what group is being defined.
configFields.notes: Free-text, must be unique. The Vendor Access tab equivalent adds a naming constraint: "It cannot be the name of any existing group name already in the system." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-tools-guides/step-3-set-up-the-named-vendor-groups-in-group-configurations-abf369db.md).

configFields.name: Attendee List Form
configFields.label: Attendee List Form
configFields.sourceQuote: Select the attendee form that should be displayed when a new attendee is added.
configFields.notes: Options are the attendee forms configured in Forms and Fields (form type Payment Request Attendee Detail View) — the corpus never enumerates them, so validValues is empty. LABEL DRIFT: the same control is called the "Forms Fields list" in a second topic (see separate entry).

configFields.name: Allow users to upload CFDi attachments
configFields.label: Allow users to upload CFDi attachments
configFields.sourceQuote: CFDi digital invoice images are required under Mexican regulatory policies. Select (enable) this setting (cleared/disabled by default) to allow users to view the CFDi Attachment command in the Actions menu and attach a digital invoice image to their invoice.
configFields.notes: Documented as cleared/disabled by default. LABEL DRIFT (singular "user"): "Select (enable) the Allow user to upload CFDi attachments check box." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-1-enable-by-invoice-group-ebe8724b.md. A third topic uses the plural form again (enabling-cfdi-attachments-for-reporting-to-mexican-tax-authorities-5ce1fd0c.md).

configFields.name: Allow Invoice Owners to create invoices
configFields.label: Allow Invoice Owners to create invoices
configFields.sourceQuote: Select this setting (the default) to allow the Invoice Owner role to create an invoice in Concur Invoice.
configFields.notes: Selected by default per the description. Historical label in the guide's revision history was "Allow Invoice Owners in Group to Create Payment Requests" (group-configuration-8b2ecb41.md, April 11 2014 row) — a matcher should tolerate the older wording.

configFields.name: Allow Invoice Owners to change vendors on assigned invoices
configFields.label: Allow Invoice Owners to change vendors on assigned invoices
configFields.sourceQuote: Select this setting to allow the Invoice Owner role to change the currently assigned vendor to a different vendor for any invoice assigned to the owner by the AP User.
configFields.notes: Scope note in the same table cell: "This applies only to those invoices not created by the Invoice Owner. If the owner created the invoice, they can change the vendor." Historical label "Allow Invoice Owners to Change Vendors" appears in the revision history (group-configuration-8b2ecb41.md).

configFields.name: Select whether vendor banking information is hidden, required, or optional for
configFields.label: Select whether vendor banking information is hidden, required, or optional for
configFields.sourceQuote: For each role, you may select an option that governs if that user is required to add banking information in the Vendor Banking Information section when requesting a new vendor.
configFields.notes: Not one control but a per-role set of selectors — one option per role. The three options ARE literally enumerated in the same table cell, so validValues is populated: "Hidden: The section does not appear, and there is nothing for the user to see or fill out." / "Required: The section appears, and all fields that must logically be filled out are marked as Required (Red highlight)." / "Optional: The section appears, but no enforcement of data entry is required unless the user fills in one or more Required fields." The corpus does not enumerate WHICH roles get a selector; it names the Invoice User and Invoice Vendor Manager roles elsewhere (concur-invoice-professional-edition-tools-guides/enabling-the-vendor-manager-to-enter-the-vendor-s-banking-information-fcb8fbdd.md).

configFields.name: Is Active for Group
configFields.label: Is Active for Group
configFields.sourceQuote: If a policy is marked as Active, it is available for inclusion into an invoice created by a member of the selected group. If a policy is marked as Inactive, it is not available.
configFields.notes: Check-box column in the Policies sub-window, one row per policy. Interaction: 'Select or clear the check box make the policy active or inactive for the new group.' (sic — verbatim, missing 'to'). Also referenced as a column heading in enable-e-bunsho-timestamp-for-a-policy-group-07ea2db1.md: 'In the Is Active for Group, check the box next to the e-Bunsho enabled policy.' policy-c8ec906b.md uses the capitalization variant 'Is Active For Group'.

configFields.name: Is Default Policy
configFields.label: Is Default Policy
configFields.sourceQuote: You will be unable to select a policy as a default if it is marked Inactive. In addition, if there is only one Active policy listed for a group, it will automatically be set to Yes in the Is Default Policy column. It cannot be changed to No until another policy available for the group is marked Active.
configFields.notes: Check-box column rendered as Yes/No in the grid. Two hard dependency rules, both structural: (1) cannot be set on a policy marked Inactive; (2) auto-forced to Yes and locked when the group has exactly one Active policy. Purpose: 'when an employee creates an invoice, the policy that appears as a default will be the one selected here.'

configFields.name: Is Inheritable
configFields.label: Is Inheritable
configFields.sourceQuote: Select or clear the check box to set whether groups below this group will inherit the group settings.
configFields.notes: Drives the hierarchy fallback: "If a group below this group does not have a configuration associated with it, and this group configuration does not allow inheritance, then when an employee creates an invoice, it will inherit policies from the group above this group rather than from this group." (same cell).

configFields.name: Policies
configFields.label: Policies (column, Modify link)
configFields.sourceQuote: Click Modify in the Policies column. The Configuration for Group window appears.
configFields.notes: Grid column on the Invoice tab whose per-row Modify link opens the policy sub-window carrying Is Active for Group / Is Default Policy / Is Inheritable. Corroborated: "On the Group Configurations page, in the Policies column, select the Modify link for a list of policies available to the group." (change-the-active-policy-d656d79c.md) and "On the Administration > Invoice > Group Configurations page in the Policies column, click Modify for the group you want to modify." (enable-e-bunsho-timestamp-for-a-policy-group-07ea2db1.md).

configFields.name: attendee type active check boxes
configFields.label: (attendee type rows in Configuration for Group)
configFields.sourceQuote: Select the check box for all attendee types that should be active for the group.
configFields.notes: One check box per attendee type inside the Attendee Types sub-window. Two structural constraints stated in the same file: "All attendee types appear except No Shows and This Employee since they are system attendee types and cannot be inactive." and "If an attendee type is set to Active at the parent group level, it will remain active at the child group level and cannot be changed to Inactive. If the attendee type is set to Inactive at the parent group level, it can be overridden at the child group level and set to Active." The set of attendee types is tenant-configured, so validValues is empty.

configFields.name: In Use
configFields.label: In Use
configFields.sourceQuote: In Use is an indicator that a group configuration is directly referred to within the overall configuration, and therefore cannot be deleted until that related configuration is updated. This does not indicate that users are assigned to the group. Some common examples of related configuration would be Company News records or conditions within Audit Rules.
configFields.notes: Read-only indicator on the list grid; gates deletability (an In Use row has no selection check box). The Group Configuration guide's revision history confirms it as a page element: "Added clarification regarding the In Use indicator." (group-configuration-8b2ecb41.md, April 22, 2022).

configFields.name: New
configFields.label: New
configFields.sourceQuote: On the Invoice tab of the Group Configurations page, select New. The Select Group window appears.
configFields.notes: Present on both tabs. Vendor Access equivalent: "Click New to open the Select Group window." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-tools-guides/step-3-set-up-the-named-vendor-groups-in-group-configurations-abf369db.md).

configFields.name: Modify
configFields.label: Modify
configFields.sourceQuote: Select the desired group configuration and click Modify. The Configuration for Group page appears.
configFields.notes: Row-level action that opens the basic Configuration for Group window. Also used read-only for viewing: "Select Modify to view the configuration." (view-group-configurations-9e1e5066.md). Distinct from the per-column Modify links in Policies and Attendee Types.

configFields.name: Delete Selected Rows
configFields.label: Delete Selected Rows
configFields.sourceQuote: Click Delete Selected Rows.
configFields.notes: Deletes the checked group configurations. Deleting the configuration does not delete the group itself: "Although an Invoice Configuration administrator can delete a group configuration, they cannot delete the group itself. Groups are defined by the source list imported into the system." (same file).

configFields.name: Select All
configFields.label: Select All
configFields.sourceQuote: Select Select All to choose all the available group configurations. Note that not all group configurations will be available for removal as they either are in use or required by Concur Invoice. These group configurations will not have associated check boxes.
configFields.notes: Bulk-select control on the Group Configurations List page; only selects rows that actually have check boxes.

configFields.name: Vendor Access tab
configFields.label: Vendor Access
configFields.sourceQuote: Click the Vendor Access tab.
configFields.notes: Second tab. Scope: "The Vendor Access tab of Group Configurations within Invoice Processing Admin is used to create those vendor groups to which you will assign vendors via import. These groups are then assigned in turn to users via User Administration to filter what vendors a user may choose from." (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/overview-8b2edfd0.md). Deep-linkable as a breadcrumb leaf (see navPathEvidence).

configFields.name: Email Alias
configFields.label: Email Alias
configFields.sourceQuote: In the Configuration for Group window, select the preferred email alias from the Email Alias list.
configFields.notes: Appears on the Vendor Access tab's Configuration for Group window, and only once Vendor Segregation is on: "Now, the functionality appears in Group Configuration > Vendor Access" (same file). Options are the aliases created in Capture Processing Admin > Email Administration, so they are tenant data and validValues stays empty.

configFields.name: Group (Vendor Access list)
configFields.label: Group
configFields.sourceQuote: In the Group list, select a vendor group, and then click Modify.
configFields.notes: Vendor group picker on the Vendor Access tab used to choose which vendor group's configuration to open. Contents are the named vendor groups created on this tab.

configFields.name: Done
configFields.label: Done
configFields.sourceQuote: Select Done. The Configuration for Group window appears.
configFields.notes: Commits the group choice in the Select Group window and advances to Configuration for Group.

configFields.name: Save
configFields.label: Save
configFields.sourceQuote: Select Save. The Group Configurations page appears.
configFields.notes: Commits the Configuration for Group window and returns to the list. Present in the basic, Policies, Attendee Types, and Vendor Access variants of the window.

configFields.name: Allow Invoice users to delete images on payment requests created on their behalf
configFields.label: Allow Invoice users to delete images on payment requests created on their behalf
configFields.sourceQuote: Select to allow the Concur Invoice user to remove images attached to invoices created by the AP User and assigned to the user. Clear (disable) to prevent the user from removing images associated with the invoice.
configFields.notes: Quote enumerates both states explicitly (Select / Clear (disable)). Default Status column in the same file: 'Enabled (selected)'. ADMIN/prevent-deletion-of-images-associated-with-an-invoice-a0521ec4.md repeats: 'The setting is selected (enabled) by default.'

configFields.name: Allow processor users to change vendor on requests pending processor roles
configFields.label: Allow processor users to change vendor on requests pending processor roles
configFields.sourceQuote: Select to allow a Processor to change the vendor associated with an invoice even during workflow steps pending a Processor. Clear (disable) to prevent the Processor from changing the vendor if the invoice is pending any Processor role in workflow (accounting review).
configFields.notes: Quote enumerates both states explicitly. Default Status column in the same file: 'Enabled (selected)'. ADMIN/prevent-processor-to-change-vendor-pending-processor-in-workflow-edbca7d1.md confirms: 'The setting is selected (enabled) by default.'

configFields.name: Allow Payment Manager to change banking information
configFields.label: Allow Payment Manager to change banking information
configFields.sourceQuote: Clear (disable) this check box to remove the Banking Import link from Payment Manager and prevent the Payment Manager role from importing any changes to banking information.
configFields.notes: Inverted-sense setting: the documented action is clearing it. Default Status column in the same file: 'Enabled (selected)'. Caution — ADMIN/prevent-changes-to-payment-manager-banking-information-4fd01601.md contains a contradiction in its prose ('If you prefer this role not have this capability, select (enable) this setting to remove the Banking Import link') while its own numbered procedure says 'clear (disable) the Allow Payment Manager to change banking information check box'. The procedure and the settings table agree; the prose sentence is an error.

configFields.name: Send vendor payment email notifications for Check and ACH Concur Invoice Pay types
configFields.label: Send vendor payment email notifications for Check and ACH Concur Invoice Pay types
configFields.sourceQuote: Select (enable) this check box if you want vendors to receive an email when they are paid via ACH or Check with Invoice Pay. The email will contain full remittance information including when, how, and for what they are paid.
configFields.notes: Default Status column in the same file: 'Disabled (cleared)'. Edition split worth capturing: TOOLS/email-remittance-notifications-ec277e48.md states 'For Standard Edition, this setting does not display in the UI but defaults to enabled.' Payment types covered are enumerated as Check and ACH; applies to both partial and full payments; Client Pay (payment outside Invoice Pay) does not trigger notifications.

configFields.name: Enable Peppol Integration
configFields.label: Enable Peppol Integration
configFields.sourceQuote: Select (enable) this check box to allow Peppol Integration and configure the feature in Concur Invoice.
configFields.notes: Default Status column in the same file: 'Disabled (cleared)'. This checkbox only unlocks the feature — actual configuration happens on a separate Peppol Configuration page (Administration > Invoice > Invoice Processing Admin > Peppol Configuration, per ADMIN/professional-edition-7e36681a.md), whose own 'Peppol Integration Enablement' field is a distinct two-value selector with values Active and Inactive (ADMIN/deactivating-peppol-integration-f8577b2a.md). ADMIN/feature-activation-04b47637.md notes the feature must first be enabled by SAP Concur staff via a service request.

configFields.name: Default payment term (days)
configFields.label: Default payment term (days)
configFields.sourceQuote: On the Invoice Settings page, input a value, in days, which will become the default payment term for all invoices not otherwise given a term within Concur Invoice.
configFields.notes: Default value is "Zero (0) days". Master table gives examples "10, 30, or 60 days" — illustrative, not an enumeration, so validValues left empty. Casing drifts to "Default Payment Term (Days)" in the topic title and "Default Payment Term (days)" in ADMIN/understanding-default-payment-terms-e71743f2.md. Overridable per vendor record and via Invoice Pay.

configFields.name: Default Discount Terms (days)
configFields.label: Default Discount Terms (days)
configFields.sourceQuote: If a discount applies, enter the NET discount terms agreed upon with the supplier.
configFields.notes: Default status "N/A". The table adds a Note: the data in this field is for information purposes only and is not used in any calculations.

configFields.name: Default discount percentage
configFields.label: Default discount percentage
configFields.sourceQuote: Enter the percentage amount (10; 15) the supplier will honor if the supplier’s discount NET terms are met.
configFields.notes: Default status "N/A". Master table states the data type constraint verbatim: "Number (11, 8) - 11 characters maximum, 8 characters maximum to the right of the decimal." Informational only, not used in calculations. Quote contains U+2019 in supplier’s.

configFields.name: Default shipping method
configFields.label: Default shipping method
configFields.sourceQuote: Select the preferred carrier for shipping. This is designated by a code representing the shipping method used by the supplier.
configFields.notes: Default status "N/A". Typed as a dropdown because the corpus verb is "Select" and the value is a code; the option list is NOT enumerated anywhere in the corpus.

configFields.name: Default shipping terms
configFields.label: Default shipping terms
configFields.sourceQuote: The code representing shipping terms with a supplier.
configFields.notes: Default status "N/A". The corpus gives no verb (no select or enter) for this control, so the widget type cannot be determined from 2026_08 text — marked unknown rather than guessed.

configFields.name: Default recurring Invoice Generation Offset
configFields.label: Default Recurring Invoice Generation Offset
configFields.sourceQuote: Use the Default Recurring Invoice Generation Offset field on the Invoice Settings page to set the number of days before the payment date that Concur Invoice automatically generates recurring invoices. The default offset is 14 days.
configFields.notes: Default value is 14 (days). Master table writes it with lowercase r as "Default recurring Invoice Generation Offset"; the dedicated topic title-cases it. Number of days before the actual billing/payment date the recurring invoice is generated.

configFields.name: Default fields that regulate duplicate invoices (Vendor is selected by default)
configFields.label: Default fields that regulate duplicate invoices (Vendor is selected by default)
configFields.sourceQuote: Use the Default fields that regulate duplicate invoices list on the Invoice Settings page to select which invoice attributes are checked alongside Vendor when the Is Duplicate audit rule runs in Concur Invoice.
configFields.notes: validValues are genuinely enumerated in this file: "Available fields are: Invoice Date / Invoice Amount / Invoice Number". Vendor is always checked and is not a selectable option. Default selection is Invoice Number (master table Default Status column). Multi-select — the file notes that to use more than one option the admin must use an AND statement when creating the Is Duplicate audit rule, and that an Is Duplicate rule must also be created in the Audit Rules tool.

configFields.name: For purchase order-based invoices, from where should the Invoice Line allocation be copied?
configFields.label: For purchase order-based invoices, from where should the Invoice Line allocation be copied?
validValues: From the associated purchase order line
configFields.sourceQuote: Use the For purchase order-based invoices, from where should the Invoice Line allocation be copied? setting on the Invoice Settings page to control whether allocation fields on invoice lines are copied from the associated purchase order line or from the existing copy-down configuration.
configFields.notes: Both options are literally enumerated as a bulleted list in this file and again in the master table. Default is "From the associated purchase order line". ADMIN/copy-down-of-po-allocation-lines-f14c45e4.md renders the second option without the hyphen as "From the copydown configurations" — tolerate both spellings. The corpus calls it a list, hence dropdown.

configDependencies.sourceQuote: Adds the PO Matching Ruleset option where PO matching rules are specified

configDependencies.sourceQuote: Now the Is Purchase Request Policy check box is exposed

configDependencies.condition: CORPUS CONFLICT, reframed from a candidate that pointed at a non-field. On a purchase request policy Bill To stops being optional and becomes required to complete the policy - directly contradicting the '(Optional)' suffix in the Create a New Policy field table. The quote sits inside the purchase-request policy topic.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Your policy will require a billing address on setup. Bill To is a required field and must be filled out to complete the policy configuration.

configDependencies.condition: Designating an Allocation Form is what activates the allocation feature; with no allocation form the Allocation Separator value is inert regardless of what is set.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Allocation Separator: This symbol separates segments of the allocation code. The default is the hyphen (-). If the allocation feature is not activated (by designating an allocation form), the separator is not used.

configDependencies.condition: Apply Auto Submit to Assignment is an optional extension inside the auto-submit condition area; it extends auto-submission from import-time to assignment-time and is meaningless without conditions set.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: (Optional) Select Apply Auto Submit to Assignment if you would like the system to automatically attempt to submit an invoice on assignment.

configDependencies.condition: ADDED IN AUDIT. Activate / Deactivate are the controls that write the Policy Status column for the selected expense types; Policy Status is not directly editable.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Select the desired expense types and click Activate or Deactivate to change the policy status.

configDependencies.condition: An expense type is unusable on the policy until its Policy Status is Active, and every newly created expense type arrives Inactive - so a freshly imported expense type will silently not appear to users.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: All new expense types appear in the Policies tool as Inactive. For the system to use an expense type in a policy, the expense type must be marked as Active.

configDependencies.condition: Setting Editable By Group(s) to Global restricts Modify to administrators of the Global group; administrators lower in the hierarchy can only copy the policy.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: If you select Global, then the information can be edited or deleted by any employee assigned to administer the Global group. Administrators assigned at lower levels in the hierarchy may copy the information but may not edit or delete it.

configDependencies.condition: Same control, second affected button: Remove (delete) is likewise limited to administrators of the group(s) named in Editable By Group(s).
configDependencies.sourceQuote: If you select Global, then the information can be edited or deleted by any employee assigned to administer the Global group. Administrators assigned at lower levels in the hierarchy may copy the information but may not edit or delete it.

configDependencies.condition: There is no create-from-scratch path. The New Policy page carrying Name is reached only by selecting an existing policy and clicking Copy Policy, so every field there defaults from the source policy.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: You can create a new policy by copying an existing one and changing the information as it applies to the new policy.

configDependencies.condition: Setting this policy field to Yes surfaces a Request New Vendor link to end users on the Create Payment Request Header page.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Selecting Yes displays a Request New Vendor link on the Create Payment Request Header page.

configDependencies.condition: Assigning an imaging configuration to the policy is what makes the View Image link appear on the Payment Request page for the Invoice Processor.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Once an imaging configuration is set up for Concur Invoice, the client must assign it to a policy. This allows employees to utilize Imaging to submit invoices electronically. The View Image link will appear on the Payment Request page and is available to the Invoice Processor.

configDependencies.condition: When the invoice's policy requires e-Bunsho timestamps, the Timestamp button appears on the invoice after it is saved (not before).
configDependencies.sourceQuote: When a user creates a new invoice, if the invoice type is set to a policy that requires e-Bunsho timestamps, after the invoice is saved, the Timestamp button appears.

configDependencies.condition: A timestamp-requiring policy holds Submit Invoice unavailable until at least one invoice image has been uploaded AND timestamped - a hard submission gate, not a warning.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Because the policy requires that invoice images be timestamped, the Submit Invoice button remains unavailable until one or more invoice images have been uploaded and timestamped.

configDependencies.condition: When the conditions set on the policy are met the system submits the invoice itself on import, and optionally on assignment.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Auto-Submission Conditions: This option lets the administrator set basic conditions that, if met, cause the invoice to be automatically submitted by the system on import and optionally on assignment.

configDependencies.condition: The Receiving feature must be switched on in the PO Configuration section of the policy before any user can enter or manage receipts in Concur Invoice.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Before users can start to work with and manage their receipts in Concur Invoice, the administrator needs to go to Administration > Invoice > Policies to activate the Receiving feature.

configDependencies.condition: Activating Concur Receiving on the policy silently puts the Purchase Order Receipt form into use - there is no separate form-assignment step to audit.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Once this feature has been activated, the Purchase Order Receipt form in the Forms and Fields tool will automatically be used.

configDependencies.condition: Two conditions, both required: at least one policy must have Is Purchase Request Policy set AND that policy must be active, before the purchase request type can be created at all.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: At least one purchase request-enabled policy must be active to create the purchase request type.

configDependencies.condition: Deleting a policy that still has forms assigned strands those forms - they are retained in the database for in-process work and become permanently undeletable. Marking the policy inactive in Group Configurations is the non-destructive alternative.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: If there are forms assigned to the policy when it is deleted, the forms will be retained in the database to handle any expense reports currently in process and will not be available for deletion.

configDependencies.condition: Deactivate the print format on the policy first; deletion on the Printed Invoices page is blocked while it is active on any policy.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: You must make the format inactive from the policy before you can delete the print format.

configDependencies.condition: A workflow cannot be deleted while any policy still references it in Invoice Workflow; the policy reference must be cleared first.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The workflow is not currently assigned to a policy. The system does not allow you to delete a workflow that is currently assigned to a policy. To delete a workflow that is currently in use, remove it from that policy.

configDependencies.condition: The Header Form dropdown is populated from Form Types, not authored on the policy; corroborated by forms-and-fields-3ed30da4.md: 'Forms are configured and made available for selection prior to creating the policy within which the forms will be assigned.'
configDependencies.sourceQuote: You create Payment Request Header Forms in the Form Types area of the Administrator.

configDependencies.condition: The Line Item Form dropdown is populated from Form Types; the form must exist before the policy can select it.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: You create Line Item Forms in the Form Types area of the Administrator.

configDependencies.condition: The Allocation Form dropdown is populated from Form Types. Note this is also the switch that activates allocation on the policy, so the Form Types build gates the whole allocation feature.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: You create Allocation Forms in the Form Types area of the Administrator.

configDependencies.condition: The Vendor Form dropdown is populated from Form Types. Label mismatch worth carrying: the field is 'Vendor Form' but the object it selects is a Vendor Address Form.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: You create Vendor Address Forms in the Form Types area of the Administrator.

configDependencies.condition: A workflow is built in Workflows and only afterwards associated to a policy. A workflow is inert until that association exists, and one workflow may serve several policies.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Once you have created the workflow, you must associate it to a policy.

configDependencies.condition: Ordered: add the scan configuration in Image Handling first, then assign it on the policy. Cardinality is explicit - one configuration may serve many policies, but a policy accepts exactly one.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: To enable and configure this feature, you must first add a scan configuration. Once you have added a scan configuration, you must assign it to a policy. One configuration can be used by multiple policies; however, each policy can only use a single scan configuration.

configDependencies.condition: The imaging configuration must be created in Image Handling before it can be selected on the policy; the policy assignment is a separate, later step.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Once an imaging configuration is set up for Concur Invoice, the client must assign it to a policy. This allows employees to utilize Imaging to submit invoices electronically. The View Image link will appear on the Payment Request page and is available to the Invoice Processor.

configDependencies.condition: Create the expense type in the Expense Types tool first; activation is then per-policy in the Policies tool. Creating it alone never makes it visible to employees.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Once you have created a new expense type, you must activate that expense type for a particular policy for it to appear to the employee in Concur Invoice. You do this within the Policies tool.

configDependencies.condition: The print format must be created or modified on the Printed Invoices page first, then assigned and activated on the policy that will use it.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Once you have modified or created a print format, you can assign it to a policy which will be used when users create invoices.

configDependencies.condition: An In Use rule set is frozen. Order is: copy it, edit the copy, then repoint the policy's PO Matching Ruleset at the copy. Alternatively strip all policy associations to unlock the original. Merged with the reverse-direction duplicate, which shared this identical quote.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: A rule set with an In Use status of Yes cannot be modified in any way. To update this rule set, use the Copy button to create a copy, edit the rule set as needed, then change the PO Matching Ruleset value in Policies to implement the new rules. Alternatively, remove all associations to the policy to allow configuration of the policy rule set selection.

configDependencies.condition: ADDED IN AUDIT. The billing address must be set up via Set a Default Shipping and Billing Address before the Bill To value exists to select, and the corpus states policy configuration cannot be completed until it is.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Refer to Setting a Default Shipping and Billing Address below to complete the billing address (as a minimum) so that policy configuration can be completed.

configDependencies.condition: Activating an expense type on a policy is gated on the Group Create right, not on reaching the page - an admin can open the list and still be unable to change Policy Status.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: You must have Group Create rights to assign the expense types to a policy.

sourceRef.field: Invoice Configuration Administrator role and group administration rights to the Policies configuration object

configDependencies.condition: Two grants must land before anyone can create a policy at all. The topic names the Global Administrator as grantor but does not name the page the grants are made on, so the source page attribution is inferred from the role model, not quoted.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The administrator must complete two configuration steps before an employee is able to create policies.

configDependencies.condition: OUT-OF-BAND PREREQUISITE, not a control on any page. Timestamp Configuration is only configurable once the tenant-level e-Bunsho Timestamp feature for Japan is enabled; a crawler finding the field absent has not found the feature switched off, it has found an un-provisioned tenant.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: When the e-Bunsho Timestamp feature for Japan is enabled, an Invoice Admin can configure policy groups that require group members to timestamp invoice images before the related invoice is submitted for approval.

configDependencies.condition: Policies must exist on the Policies page before they can be assigned to a group, and the assignment itself is performed in Group Configurations, never on Policies. Merged from two duplicate candidates drawn from this same file.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Once you have created your policies, you must assign them to a group. Use Group Configurations in the Administration menu to complete the assignment.

configDependencies.condition: The Applies to column on Policies is read-only reporting of what was written in Group Configurations. Editing group scope from the Policies page is not possible, so a crawler must not treat this column as a control.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: actual assignment of the policy to a group occurs in the Group Configurations area

configDependencies.condition: ADDED IN AUDIT. The value rendered in the Policies page Applies to column is a function of Is Inheritable: with inheritance on it covers the named group plus every group beneath it, with inheritance off only the named group. The column is therefore not a literal list of assigned groups.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: If inheritance applies, then the configuration applies to the group(s) listed in the Group column of the Group Configurations page, and all groups that are beneath the identified group, in the hierarchical structure.

configDependencies.condition: Two-phase: set Timestamp Configuration to Japan e-Bunsho on the policy first, then activate that e-Bunsho-enabled policy for the group. Merged from two duplicate candidates; kept the quote that actually states the ordering dependency rather than the procedure title.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: In the Is Active for Group, check the box next to the e-Bunsho enabled policy.

configDependencies.condition: Rule 1 of 3 on this pair: a policy whose Is Active for Group box is cleared cannot be selected as the group default.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: You will be unable to select a policy as a default if it is marked Inactive.

configDependencies.condition: Rule 2 of 3: when exactly one policy is Active for the group the system forces Is Default Policy to Yes and locks it. An auditor seeing Yes here has not necessarily seen a deliberate choice.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: if there is only one Active policy listed for a group, it will automatically be set to Yes in the Is Default Policy column. It cannot be changed to No until another policy available for the group is marked Active.

configDependencies.condition: Rule 3 of 3: once more than one policy is assigned to the group, naming a default becomes mandatory rather than optional. Source reframed from a non-field candidate ('Number of policies assigned to a group'); the quote says 'assigned to a group', and Is Active for Group is the control that performs that assignment.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: If more than one policy is assigned to a group, then the administrator must specify one of the policies as the default policy (to be used if the employee does not select a policy).

targetRef.field: policy availability on a new invoice

configDependencies.condition: Marking the policy Active for the group is what puts it in reach of that group's members at invoice creation; Inactive removes it. Merged from two duplicate candidates.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: If a policy is marked as Active, it is available for inclusion into an invoice created by a member of the selected group. If a policy is marked as Inactive, it is not available.

configDependencies.condition: Clearing Is Inheritable pushes child groups that have no configuration of their own PAST this group - they inherit from the level above instead. Merged from two duplicate candidates sharing this quote.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: If a group below this group does not have a configuration associated with it, and this group configuration does not allow inheritance, then when an employee creates an invoice, it will inherit policies from the group above this group rather than from this group.

configDependencies.condition: Omitting a group configuration is itself a configuration decision - the undefined group silently inherits from the next defined level up. Absence of a row is not absence of policy.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: If you do not define a group, then it will inherit from the next level that is defined. You always inherit the policy for undefined groups.

configDependencies.condition: Saving a new group configuration is not sufficient; the Policies (and Payment Types) columns must then be edited to declare which are active for that group.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: However, to create a new group, you must edit the policies and payment types to define which ones are active for that group.

configDependencies.condition: Reframed from a candidate that attributed the source to Audit Rules, which the quote does not name. A row flagged In Use is referenced elsewhere in the configuration, has no selection check box, and cannot be deleted until the referencing configuration is changed.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: In Use is an indicator that a group configuration is directly referred to within the overall configuration, and therefore cannot be deleted until that related configuration is updated.

configDependencies.condition: Deleting a group configuration does not orphan its employees - they immediately fall back to the nearest ancestor group with a corresponding policy, up to the Global Group.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Once a group configuration is deleted, the employees contained within the deleted group will now inherit the policies of whatever group above has a corresponding policy in place, all the way up to the Global Group if required.

configDependencies.condition: Reframed to keep both endpoints on the audited page. Delete Selected Rows removes only the configuration, never the group - groups originate from the imported source list and must be removed there.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Although an Invoice Configuration administrator can delete a group configuration, they cannot delete the group itself.

configDependencies.condition: Distinct from the import-link effect: to force banking changes through the ERP / Vendor Master List instead of on-demand, the Invoice Processing Admin must clear this option first. The Payment Manager lockdown is the consequence, not a separate control.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Your company can turn off the ability to update banking details on-demand in Payment Manager. To do this, Invoice Processing Admins must clear (disable) the Allow Payment Manager to change banking information option in Invoice Settings.

configDependencies.condition: Direction set so the Invoice Settings control is the source. No remittance email is ever sent unless this check box is selected; default is cleared in Professional Edition.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: For vendors to receive these emails, you must select the Send vendor payment email notifications for Check and ACH Concur Invoice Pay types option on the Invoice Settings page.

sourceRef.field: Send vendor payment email notifications for Check and ACH Concur Invoice Pay types

configDependencies.condition: The setting only produces mail if the vendor record carries an address in the Vendor Contact field of the Approved Vendor Import; only one address is supported. Enabling the toggle against an empty Vendor Contact yields silence.

sourceRef.field: Send vendor payment email notifications for Check and ACH Concur Invoice Pay types

configDependencies.sourceQuote: Payment of invoices that occur outside of Invoice Pay (Client Pay) do not trigger email notifications.

configDependencies.condition: OUT-OF-BAND PREREQUISITE, not a control on this or any page - it is a support service request. The Enable Peppol Integration check box does not exist for the tenant until SAP Concur staff turn the feature on, so a crawler finding it absent has not found it disabled.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The Peppol Integration feature for Concur Invoice must be enabled by SAP Concur staff. Clients must initiate a service request with SAP Concur support.

configDependencies.condition: The Invoice Settings check box (default cleared) only allows Peppol Integration; the actual field-level configuration is then done separately on the Peppol Configuration page.

configDependencies.condition: Direction set so the Invoice Settings control is the source. CROSS-MODULE VALUE CONSTRAINT: once Peppol Integration is in use, Ledger Name on the Accounting Structure tab is pinned to the literal value 'Default'.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Customers using Peppol Integration must always set the Ledger Name as "Default".

configDependencies.sourceQuote: The Invoice Admin can deny the Invoice User role the ability to delete an image from an invoice created for them. By default, the user can delete the image.

configDependencies.condition: Selected (enabled) by default. The restriction is workflow-state scoped, not blanket: clearing it blocks the Processor from changing the vendor only while the invoice is pending ANY Processor role in workflow.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Select to allow a Processor to change the vendor associated with an invoice even during workflow steps pending a Processor. Clear (disable) to prevent the Processor from changing the vendor if the invoice is pending any Processor role in workflow (accounting review).

configDependencies.sourceQuote: If clients select the From the associated purchase order line option, PO allocations lines will automatically be copied down from the PO line to the associated invoice line.

sourceRef.field: For purchase order-based invoices, from where should the Invoice Line allocation be copied?
