Choosing this value with no copydown configuration in place produces no copy-down at all. Spelling drift: rendered 'From the copydown configurations' in one topic.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: If clients select the From the copy-down configurations option, the copydown configuration of allocation fields will apply to both PO-based and non-PO based invoices.

sourceRef.field: For purchase order-based invoices, from where should the Invoice Line allocation be copied?

configDependencies.condition: PRECEDENCE, distinct from the deferral rule above. Set to From the associated purchase order line, this Invoice Settings value overrides the Forms and Fields copydown configuration for PO-based invoices - so a Forms and Fields change will appear to have no effect.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: With this setting, clients can copy down PO allocation lines regardless of the copydown configuration.

configSteps.name: Create a new invoice policy and make it selectable by a group
configSteps.goal: A new, correctly-formed invoice policy exists with its forms, workflow, image handling and expense types set, and members of at least one group can actually pick it when they create an invoice (it is Active for the group, with a default settled).

sequence.action: select the row of an existing policy to use as the base
sequence.rationale: There is no blank-form creation path in 2026_08: creation IS copying, so a base row must be selected before the Copy Policy button has anything to act on. SOURCE: "You can create a new policy by copying an existing one and changing the information as it applies to the new policy." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md

sequence.action: click
sequence.rationale: This is what opens the editable New Policy page; every field below only exists after this click. Every dropdown also arrives pre-filled from the copied policy, which is why the following steps are edits, not first-time entries. SOURCE: "Select Copy Policy." and "The New Policy page appears." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md

sequence.action: clear and type the new policy name
sequence.rationale: Rename first. The copy inherits the base policy's name, and every later corpus procedure addresses a policy as "the desired policy" on a list keyed by name — two same-named rows make Modify, Expense Types, Print Format and the Group Configurations assignment ambiguous. Ordering-within-the-page here is inference; the corpus only fixes Name as the first row of the field table. SOURCE: "Enter a name for the new policy." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md

sequence.action: select the header form
sequence.rationale: A precondition outside this page, not an ordering choice on it: the option list is built elsewhere, so the form must already exist in Form Types before the writer arrives here. Selecting a name that has not been created yet is unrecoverable from this page. SOURCE: "You create Payment Request Header Forms in the Form Types area of the Administrator." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md

sequence.action: select the line item form
sequence.rationale: Same external precondition as Header Form — the Line Item Form must pre-exist in Form Types. Grouped with the other form bindings because the corpus describes the policy as a container of exactly these four forms. SOURCE: "Select the Line Item Form to be associated with the new policy." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md

sequence.action: select the allocation form (or deliberately leave it unset)
sequence.rationale: Must come BEFORE Allocation Separator, and this is a corpus-stated dependency, not a guess: designating an allocation form is what turns the allocation feature on, and the separator is dead until it is. Leaving this unset is a real decision — it disables allocation for the policy. SOURCE: "Allocation Separator: This symbol separates segments of the allocation code. The default is the hyphen (-). If the allocation feature is not activated (by designating an allocation form), the separator is not used." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/components-of-the-policy-3bf075f8.md

sequence.action: select the separator symbol
sequence.rationale: Sits after Allocation Form for the reason above: set before an allocation form exists and the value is inert, so a writer that sets it first cannot tell whether it took. Default is the hyphen, so skipping it is safe. SOURCE: "Allocation Separator: This symbol separates segments of the allocation code. The default is the hyphen (-)." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/components-of-the-policy-3bf075f8.md

sequence.action: select the vendor address form
sequence.rationale: Must precede the new-vendor-request toggle below, because that toggle exposes a request path that renders this form to the employee. Label on screen is Vendor Form; the object it names is a Vendor Address Form. SOURCE: "Select the Vendor Address Form to be associated with the new policy." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md

sequence.action: select Yes to permit employee-initiated vendor requests
sequence.rationale: Placed after both Vendor Form and Header Form because selecting Yes adds a link to the Create Payment Request Header page — the surfaces it depends on should already be bound. The corpus does not state this ordering; it is inference from the documented downstream effect. Note this is a Yes-valued selector, not a check box. SOURCE: "Select Yes to allow an employee to request a new vendor be added to the master vendor list." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md

sequence.action: select or clear the check box
sequence.rationale: Order-independent within the General page — nothing else on the page reads it — so it belongs among the late General-page toggles rather than early where it would consume a decision the writer may not have an answer for yet. Label carries a trailing colon in the corpus. SOURCE: "Select this check box if you want to allow the Invoice User to have privileges to re-assign an invoice they have unassigned from themselves." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md

sequence.action: select the workflow
sequence.rationale: Another pre-existence dependency outside this page: workflows are built in the Workflows area, so the target workflow must be published before the policy can point at it. Reuse is explicitly allowed, so a writer should not create a new workflow just because it is creating a new policy. SOURCE: "You create invoice workflows in the Workflows area of the Administrator." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md and "A workflow can be assigned to multiple policies." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/implementation-guidelines-for-policies-0c35d480.md

sequence.action: select the scan configuration, or knowingly leave it blank
sequence.rationale: Has no default, and the failure is silent: an unset value simply means scan never works for this policy, with no error to catch it later. The configuration must already exist on the Scan Configurations page in Image Handling, and one policy can hold only one. SOURCE: "Select a scan configuration to be associated with this policy. There is no default value assigned; if you do not select a configuration, the scan functionality will not be active for the policy." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md; corroborated "One configuration can be used by multiple policies; however, each policy can only use a single scan configuration." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/step-2-assign-the-scan-configuration-to-a-policy-634c76ba.md

sequence.action: select the imaging configuration, or knowingly leave it blank
sequence.rationale: Same silent-failure shape as Scan Configuration, and it gates a visible downstream control (the View Image link for the Invoice Processor), so it must be decided here rather than discovered missing during processor testing. SOURCE: "Select an imaging configuration to be associated with this policy. There is no default value assigned; if you do not select a configuration, the imaging functionality will not be active for the policy." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md

sequence.action: select the owning group(s)
sequence.rationale: Set while still on the General page, because it decides who may reopen this policy at all — get it wrong and the writer can lock itself (or the intended group admin) out of every later Modify. The admin's own rights cap the choice, so Global may not be offerable. This is scope-to-EDIT only; it does not make the policy usable by anyone, which is why order 20 onward is mandatory. SOURCE: "Select the group(s) for which an administrator must have administration rights to modify the policy." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md

sequence.action: add the default billing address
sequence.rationale: Labelled Optional on this wizard, so it is safe to defer for a plain payment policy — but see step g1-s2: for a purchase-request policy the same field is required and blocks completion. A writer should treat 'Optional' as conditional, not absolute. SOURCE: "Add a default Bill To address to associate with new invoices." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md

sequence.action: advance the wizard (Next) to the Expense Types for Policy step and read the copied rows
sequence.rationale: The General page must be complete before advancing, because the wizard does not return here on its own — later access is via the Modify button on the Policies list, a different entry point. The expense-type rows arrive copied from the base policy, so they are inherited state to audit, not a blank list. SOURCE: "The Expense Types for Policy step appears." and "This information is copied directly from the policy that you selected as the base for the new policy" — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md

sequence.action: read the per-row status before changing anything
sequence.rationale: This is the step most likely to be skipped and the most damaging to skip. Only Active expense types reach the employee's Expense Type list, and anything newly created lands Inactive — so a policy that looks finished can be unusable. Two values only: Active, Inactive. SOURCE: "All new expense types appear in the Policies tool as Inactive. For the system to use an expense type in a policy, the expense type must be marked as Active." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/expense-types-and-policies-a01e2537.md

sequence.action: multi-select the required expense types, then click
sequence.rationale: Acts on the current selection, so selection must precede the click — Shift+click / Ctrl+click builds the set in one pass, which matters because the button is applied per selection, not per row. Tolerate the label typo: one topic writes "Select Active or Deactivate." SOURCE: "Select the desired expense types and click Activate or Deactivate to change the policy status." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md; corroborated "Select the expense types to modify. You can select individual expense types or use Shift+click or Ctrl+click to select multiple expense types." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/change-the-status-of-an-expense-type-cf452b6a.md

sequence.action: advance to the Auto Submit Conditions step and add a condition row
sequence.rationale: Optional, and deliberately after expense types: auto-submit fires on import, so switching it on before the expense-type set is correct means the first imported invoices submit against a half-configured policy. The corpus does not enumerate the operators or operands in this editor, so a writer must be handed the condition, not guess it. SOURCE: "(Optional) If you would like to configure and use auto submit conditions, select Insert, and then enter the conditions that you want." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md

sequence.action: select the check box inside the Auto Submit Conditions area
sequence.rationale: Only meaningful once a condition row exists (order 19), which is why it sits after Insert rather than beside it. It widens the trigger from import-only to assignment as well. SOURCE: "Auto-Submission Conditions: This option lets the administrator set basic conditions that, if met, cause the invoice to be automatically submitted by the system on import and optionally on assignment." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/components-of-the-policy-3bf075f8.md

sequence.action: advance to the Print Formats step and select the format, then commit the wizard
sequence.rationale: Last step of the wizard, and the terminal commit lives here — the corpus's final instruction is "Select Done.", which saves everything from orders 3-21 in one write, so abandoning the wizard earlier loses the whole policy. (No Done/Save control appears in the verified Policies field set, so it is named here in rationale rather than emitted as a field.) Default reports are conditional on being activated in this tool. SOURCE: "(Optional) If you want to configure and use print formats, select the print format that you want to use for the policy." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md; corroborated "NOTE: Any custom report that the admin creates will display for the user if the admin has activated the report in the Policies tool. Default reports are the only conditional reports." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/assign-a-print-format-to-a-policy-6bd703e7.md

sequence.action: on the group's row, click the Modify link in the Policies column
sequence.rationale: The hard page boundary of this outcome, stated outright by the corpus: creating the policy does not deploy it. Nothing an employee does changes until this sub-window is opened, and the Applies to / Editable By columns back on the Policies page are read-only reflections of what happens here. Cannot be done before order 21 — the policy row must exist in this list first. SOURCE: "Once you have created your policies, you must assign them to a group." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/assign-a-policy-to-a-group-f9adaed6.md; corroborated "On the Group Configurations page, in the Policies column, select the Modify link for a list of policies available to the group." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/change-the-active-policy-d656d79c.md

sequence.action: select the check box on the new policy's row
sequence.rationale: MUST precede Is Default Policy — this is an explicit corpus constraint, not an inference: an Inactive policy cannot be made the default, so a writer that reaches for the default column first simply finds it unavailable. This check box is also what makes the policy selectable at all. SOURCE: "If a policy is marked as Active, it is available for inclusion into an invoice created by a member of the selected group. If a policy is marked as Inactive, it is not available." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/add-groups-ec5d8d8b.md

sequence.action: select or verify the check box in the Is Default Policy column
sequence.rationale: After activation, for the reason in order 23. Two traps a writer must expect rather than treat as failure: with exactly one Active policy the value is forced to Yes and cannot be set back to No, and with more than one Active policy a default MUST be nominated. SOURCE: "You will be unable to select a policy as a default if it is marked Inactive. In addition, if there is only one Active policy listed for a group, it will automatically be set to Yes in the Is Default Policy column." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/add-groups-ec5d8d8b.md; corroborated "If more than one policy is assigned to a group, then the administrator must specify one of the policies as the default policy (to be used if the employee does not select a policy)." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/implementation-guidelines-for-policies-0c35d480.md

sequence.action: click to commit the policy sub-window
sequence.rationale: Terminal commit for orders 22-24; the sub-window's changes are not live until this returns to the list page. Only after this does the outcome hold end-to-end. SOURCE: "Select Save. The Group Configurations page appears." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/add-groups-ec5d8d8b.md

configSteps.name: Stand up a PO / purchase-request policy with matching and receiving
configSteps.goal: A purchase-order-enabled policy (optionally purchase-request-enabled) exists with its PO forms, matching rule set and receiving switched on, its required billing address filled, and it is Active for a group so employees can raise purchase requests and PO-matched invoices.

sequence.action: select the existing Payment Request Policy row as the base
sequence.rationale: The corpus is unusually emphatic that the PR/PO policy must be derived from the existing default rather than built fresh — copying carries the working form and workflow bindings that a from-scratch attempt would have to reconstruct. SOURCE: "It is critical that the existing default policy be copied and then configured for PR/PO as described below. Select the Payment Request Policy, then click Copy Policy and rename the copied policy, for example, Purchase Request Policy." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/policy-c8ec906b.md

sequence.action: click
sequence.rationale: Same reason as the plain-policy flow: this is the only documented route to an editable new policy page. SOURCE: "Select the Payment Request Policy, then click Copy Policy and rename the copied policy, for example, Purchase Request Policy." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/policy-c8ec906b.md

sequence.action: rename the copy
sequence.rationale: The corpus names the rename as part of the copy instruction itself, not a later cleanup — a PO policy that still carries the payment policy's name is indistinguishable on the Policies list and in the Group Configurations policy grid, where the group assignment in orders 15-17 is made by name. SOURCE: "click Copy Policy and rename the copied policy, for example, Purchase Request Policy." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/policy-c8ec906b.md

sequence.action: select the check box
sequence.rationale: THE ordering fact for this whole step, and the corpus says it in so many words: this box is selected FIRST because every PO control below — the PO forms, PO Matching Ruleset, Enable Concur Receiving, and the Is Purchase Request Policy box itself — does not exist on the page until it is checked. A writer that tries to set PO Matching Ruleset before this will not find the control. It is also effectively one-way: it cannot be cleared once invoices exist under the policy. SOURCE: "Since the purchase request is associated to a purchase order, the Is PO Policy check box is first selected:" — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/policy-c8ec906b.md; corroborated "Is PO Policy: Select this option to define the policy as PO-related. This selection causes the page to display additional options used under the PO policy and will ensure match rules run for any invoices associated with this policy." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/purchase-order-policy-fields-4aa0ac1b.md

sequence.action: select the check box (only if purchase requests are needed)
sequence.rationale: Second-level conditional: it is EXPOSED by order 4 and in turn reveals the Purchase Request Configuration group. Two conditionals deep means a writer must re-read the page after each check rather than assume a fixed field set. Skip this and you get a PO-matching policy but no purchase requests. SOURCE: "Now the Is Purchase Request Policy check box is exposed and, when selected, displays the Purchase Request Configuration options (forms and workflow selections) as shown in the figure above." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/policy-c8ec906b.md

sequence.action: select the PO header form
sequence.rationale: Revealed by order 4 and treated exactly like the standard forms, so the same external precondition applies: the PO form types must already exist before they can be bound here. SOURCE: "Selecting Require PO Matching adds the following form fields - refer to the descriptions above, PO form types act just as standard forms:" — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md

sequence.action: select the PO line item form
sequence.rationale: Same reveal and same precondition as PO Header Form; grouped with it so the three PO form bindings are set in one pass while the conditional section is open. SOURCE: "Selecting Require PO Matching adds the following form fields - refer to the descriptions above, PO form types act just as standard forms:" — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md

sequence.action: select the PO allocation form
sequence.rationale: Completes the PO form set, and should precede any allocation copy-down expectation: the tenant-wide copy-down choice on Invoice Settings (see step g1-s4) has nothing to copy into unless PO allocation is formed here. That cross-page link is inference from the two fields' descriptions, not a corpus instruction. SOURCE: "Selecting Require PO Matching adds the following form fields - refer to the descriptions above, PO form types act just as standard forms:" — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md

sequence.action: select the matching rule set
sequence.rationale: Only appears on a PO policy, so it is strictly after order 4. The rule set itself is built in Purchase Order Matching Rules and must pre-exist; the option list is tenant-authored and is not enumerated anywhere in 2026_08, so a writer must be given the rule set name. Rule sets are per-policy, so a second PO policy needs its own decision here rather than inheriting one. SOURCE: "Adds the PO Matching Ruleset option where PO matching rules are specified" — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md; corroborated "PO Matching Ruleset: This is where you specify the matching rule set that will instruct the system how to react whenever a user-defined variance is detected between the matching invoice and PO." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/purchase-order-policy-fields-4aa0ac1b.md

sequence.action: select the option in the PO Configuration section
sequence.rationale: Placed after the PO forms because activating it changes form behaviour on its own: the Purchase Order Receipt form in Forms and Fields is then adopted automatically, so a writer setting forms afterwards may be fighting an auto-selection it did not make. This is what turns on manual quantity receipts and three-way matching. SOURCE: "In the PO Configuration section of the page that appears, select the Enable Concur Receiving option." and "Once this feature has been activated, the Purchase Order Receipt form in the Forms and Fields tool will automatically be used." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/configure-concur-receiving-1ececc23.md

sequence.action: select the billing address
sequence.rationale: Do not trust the '(Optional)' in the label — the corpus directly contradicts it for this policy type and says the configuration cannot be completed without it, so this is a blocker, not a nicety. It must be filled before attempting to commit the policy, and the addresses themselves are maintained by the separate Set a Default Shipping and Billing Address procedure, which therefore has to be done first. SOURCE: "Your policy will require a billing address on setup. Bill To is a required field and must be filled out to complete the policy configuration." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/policy-c8ec906b.md

sequence.action: leave the system value in place unless an external identifier must match
sequence.rationale: Deliberately late and deliberately usually untouched: it is system-generated, must stay unique, and is the key the system uses to associate the policy with invoices and POs — editing it after invoices exist breaks that association. Only change it when an inbound PO feed dictates the value. SOURCE: "External ID: This unique identifier lets the system associate the policy to all invoices and POs that include this same identifier." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/purchase-order-policy-fields-4aa0ac1b.md

sequence.action: confirm or change the suggested workflow
sequence.rationale: Checked after order 4 rather than before it, because turning on Is PO Policy offers its own suggested default workflow — a writer that sets the workflow first may see its choice replaced. The suggestion is changeable. SOURCE: "Offers suggested default PO forms and workflow (this can be changed)" — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md

sequence.action: select the owning group(s), then commit the policy
sequence.rationale: Last field on the General page, and the last chance to get edit-scope right before the policy is committed; the admin's own rights limit what can be picked. The commit itself is the wizard's Done / the Modify page's Save — named here because no such control appears in the verified Policies field set. SOURCE: "Select the group(s) for which an administrator must have administration rights to modify the policy." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md

sequence.action: on the target group's row, click the Modify link in the Policies column
sequence.rationale: Page switch, and the corpus is explicit that this is not optional for PR policies — without it employees cannot create a purchase request at all, no matter how complete the policy is. Must follow order 14 so the policy appears in this grid. SOURCE: "Be sure to assign the PR policy to an existing Group so that the employee can create a purchase request. To do this, click Group Configurations, select the policy, and then click Modify under Policies in the Group Configurations tool." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/policy-c8ec906b.md

sequence.action: select the check box on the PR/PO policy's row
sequence.rationale: The step that actually enables the purchase-request type — the corpus states the requirement as a system precondition, not a preference. Also precedes the default column for the same Inactive-cannot-be-default reason as the plain policy flow. Tolerate the capitalisation variant 'Is Active For Group'. SOURCE: "At least one purchase request-enabled policy must be active to create the purchase request type." and "In the Configuration for Group window, select the check box in the Is Active For Group column. This associates the PR policy to the working Group, and allows users to create the invoice that uses the PR policy." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/policy-c8ec906b.md

sequence.action: optionally select the check box in the Is Default Policy column
sequence.rationale: After activation, per the constraint in order 16. Expect it to be forced to Yes if this is now the group's only Active policy — that is documented behaviour, not a write failure. SOURCE: "(Optional) Check the box in the Is Default Policy column to make the e-Bunsho policy the default policy for this group." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/enable-e-bunsho-timestamp-for-a-policy-group-07ea2db1.md

sequence.action: click to commit the policy sub-window
sequence.rationale: Terminal commit for orders 15-17; until it returns to the Group Configurations page the group cannot use the policy. SOURCE: "Select Save. The Group Configurations page appears." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/add-groups-ec5d8d8b.md

configSteps.name: Create a group configuration and pin its policies, attendees and inheritance
configSteps.goal: A group whose invoice behaviour differs from its parent has its own configuration: named, with Invoice Owner permissions and vendor-banking visibility set, its usable policies marked Active with a default nominated, its attendee types scoped, and inheritance to child groups decided explicitly.
fields: Allow users to upload CFDi attachments
Allow Invoice Owners to create invoices
Allow Invoice Owners to change vendors on assigned invoices
Select whether vendor banking information is hidden, required, or optional for

sequence.action: on the Invoice tab, click
sequence.rationale: Before clicking, confirm this group needs its own row at all — the corpus's guidance is to create a configuration ONLY where the group's policy/audit/reminder data differs, because undefined groups inherit from the level above and every extra row is maintenance. Available groups are also capped by the admin's own rights (own group and below, never a peer or a parent). SOURCE: "You only create group configurations for groups where the payment policy, audit rules, and email reminders information is different for a particular group of employees." and "You can only create group configurations for groups for which you are assigned rights and for groups below those groups." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/add-groups-ec5d8d8b.md

sequence.action: pick the group in the Select Group window
sequence.rationale: The group is chosen in a modal, not typed into the form — so this happens before any field on the Configuration for Group window is reachable. Choosing the wrong level here is the expensive error: it decides which employees the whole configuration governs. SOURCE: "On the Invoice tab of the Group Configurations page, select New. The Select Group window appears." and "Select the correct group as it should appear within the other tools and to the employee." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/add-groups-ec5d8d8b.md

sequence.action: click
sequence.rationale: Commits the group choice and is what opens the Configuration for Group window — a distinct control from the Save at order 9, and confusing the two loses the field entries. SOURCE: "Select Done. The Configuration for Group window appears." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/add-groups-ec5d8d8b.md

sequence.action: type a unique descriptive name
sequence.rationale: First field, and the corpus gives the reason it matters more than it looks: other configuration tools show this NAME, not the group path, so a vague name makes every later cross-tool selection guesswork. Must be unique — the Vendor Access variant states it cannot duplicate any existing group name in the system. SOURCE: "Type a unique name that describes this group. When creating other configurations, you will see the group name and not the group path, so make sure it is descriptive of what group is being defined." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/add-groups-ec5d8d8b.md; corroborated "It cannot be the name of any existing group name already in the system." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-tools-guides/step-3-set-up-the-named-vendor-groups-in-group-configurations-abf369db.md

sequence.action: select the attendee form
sequence.rationale: External precondition: the form is authored in Forms and Fields, so it must exist before it can be bound. Set it before the attendee-type work at order 14 — the form is what renders when a new attendee is added, so scoping types against no form leaves nothing to display. That ordering is inference from the two descriptions. Tolerate the label drift: a second topic calls this the 'Forms Fields list'. SOURCE: "Select the attendee form that should be displayed when a new attendee is added." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/add-groups-ec5d8d8b.md

sequence.action: select the check box only if the group is subject to Mexican CFDi requirements
sequence.field: Allow users to upload CFDi attachments
sequence.rationale: Cleared by default, so it is an opt-in per group rather than a tenant-wide switch — which is exactly why it belongs on this page and not in Invoice Settings. Matchers must tolerate the singular label 'Allow user to upload CFDi attachments' used in another topic. SOURCE: "Select (enable) this setting (cleared/disabled by default) to allow users to view the CFDi Attachment command in the Actions menu and attach a digital invoice image to their invoice." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/add-groups-ec5d8d8b.md

sequence.action: confirm or clear the check box
sequence.field: Allow Invoice Owners to create invoices
sequence.rationale: Selected by default, so this is a decision to LEAVE ON or turn off — a writer that treats it as an empty box to tick will misread the state. It must be settled before order 8, because the vendor-change permission only has meaning for owners who participate in invoices at all. Historical label 'Allow Invoice Owners in Group to Create Payment Requests' may still appear. SOURCE: "Select this setting (the default) to allow the Invoice Owner role to create an invoice in Concur Invoice." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/add-groups-ec5d8d8b.md

sequence.action: select or clear the check box
sequence.field: Allow Invoice Owners to change vendors on assigned invoices
sequence.rationale: Narrower than it reads, and the scope note is the load-bearing part: it governs only invoices the owner did NOT create — owners can always change the vendor on their own invoices, so clearing this does not lock vendors down as tightly as a writer might assume. SOURCE: "This applies only to those invoices not created by the Invoice Owner. If the owner created the invoice, they can change the vendor." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/add-groups-ec5d8d8b.md

sequence.action: set the option for each role listed
sequence.field: Select whether vendor banking information is hidden, required, or optional for
sequence.rationale: Not one control but one selector PER ROLE, so a writer must iterate the rendered rows rather than write a single value; the corpus does not enumerate which roles get a selector, only the three options each takes (Hidden, Required, Optional). Choosing Required here is what forces banking data at new-vendor-request time, so it must be decided before the group starts requesting vendors. SOURCE: "For each role, you may select an option that governs if that user is required to add banking information in the Vendor Banking Information section when requesting a new vendor." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/add-groups-ec5d8d8b.md

sequence.action: click to commit the basic Configuration for Group window
sequence.rationale: Hard boundary in the corpus's own numbering: the basic window is saved and returns to the list page BEFORE the Policies column is touched. The per-column Modify links act on a saved row, so attempting orders 11-13 without this save has nothing to act on. SOURCE: "Select Save. The Group Configurations page appears." followed by "Click Modify in the Policies column. The Configuration for Group window appears." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/add-groups-ec5d8d8b.md

sequence.action: click the Modify link in the Policies column for this group
sequence.rationale: Mandatory, not optional — the corpus states that a new group is not finished until its policies are edited to define which are active for it. A group saved at order 10 and left here has no usable policy set. SOURCE: "However, to create a new group, you must edit the policies and payment types to define which ones are active for that group." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/access-the-group-configurations-tool-6f974fe5.md

sequence.action: select the check box on each policy the group may use
sequence.rationale: Comes before the default column because an Inactive policy cannot be made default. Also the documented soft-delete route for retiring a policy that cannot be removed: clear it here rather than deleting the policy, since deletion strands its forms in the database permanently. SOURCE: "Select or clear the check box make the policy active or inactive for the new group." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/add-groups-ec5d8d8b.md; corroborated "You can, however, mark this policy as Inactive in Group Configurations so it is no longer available for future selection." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/delete-a-policy-700569c5.md

sequence.action: select or verify the check box in the Is Default Policy column
sequence.rationale: Strictly after order 12, and required as soon as more than one policy is Active for the group — otherwise employees who do not pick a policy have no defined behaviour. Rendered Yes/No; forced to Yes and locked when only one Active policy exists. SOURCE: "You will be unable to select a policy as a default if it is marked Inactive. In addition, if there is only one Active policy listed for a group, it will automatically be set to Yes in the Is Default Policy column. It cannot be changed to No until another policy available for the group is marked Active." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/add-groups-ec5d8d8b.md

sequence.action: select or clear the check box, then Save the sub-window
sequence.rationale: Set LAST inside the policy sub-window, because it publishes everything decided in orders 12-13 downward — and the failure mode if it is wrong is silent and counter-intuitive: an un-inheritable configuration does not make child groups fall back to nothing, it makes them inherit from the group ABOVE this one, skipping the configuration just built. SOURCE: "If a group below this group does not have a configuration associated with it, and this group configuration does not allow inheritance, then when an employee creates an invoice, it will inherit policies from the group above this group rather than from this group." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/add-groups-ec5d8d8b.md

sequence.action: open the Attendee Types column's Modify link and select the check box for each type that should be active
sequence.rationale: Do the PARENT group before any child group — the asymmetry is explicit and one-way: a type set Active at the parent stays active at the child and cannot be turned off there, whereas Inactive at the parent CAN be overridden to Active at the child. So over-activating at the parent is unrecoverable from the child. Expect No Shows and This Employee to be absent; they are system types and cannot be made inactive. The type set itself is tenant-configured. SOURCE: "If an attendee type is set to Active at the parent group level, it will remain active at the child group level and cannot be changed to Inactive. If the attendee type is set to Inactive at the parent group level, it can be overridden at the child group level and set to Active." and "All attendee types appear except No Shows and This Employee since they are system attendee types and cannot be inactive." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/procedure-configure-attendee-types-by-user-groups-4a865d21.md

sequence.action: read the indicator on the finished row before any later cleanup attempt
sequence.rationale: Last, and read-only — worth capturing at the end because it determines whether this configuration can ever be deleted: an In Use row has no selection check box, so Delete Selected Rows cannot reach it. Note also that deleting a configuration would never delete the group itself, which comes from the imported source list. SOURCE: "Although an Invoice Configuration administrator can delete a group configuration, they cannot delete the group itself. Groups are defined by the source list imported into the system." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/add-groups-ec5d8d8b.md

configSteps.name: Set tenant-wide invoice defaults before policies and groups go live
configSteps.goal: The site-wide Invoice Settings page is deliberately set for a new tenant: payment and discount terms, recurring-generation lead time, the duplicate-detection basis, PO allocation copy-down source, and the role restrictions whose defaults are permissive — so that group- and policy-level work later inherits sane values instead of accidental ones.
fields: Default fields that regulate duplicate invoices (Vendor is selected by default)
For purchase order-based invoices, from where should the Invoice Line allocation be copied?
Allow Invoice users to delete images on payment requests created on their behalf
Allow processor users to change vendor on requests pending processor roles
Allow Payment Manager to change banking information
Send vendor payment email notifications for Check and ACH Concur Invoice Pay types

sequence.action: enter the standard number of days
sequence.rationale: First because its default is the one most likely to be wrong and least likely to error: zero days, meaning every invoice with no explicit term is due immediately. It applies tenant-wide unless overridden on the invoice or through Invoice Pay, so setting it before any invoices flow avoids retroactive term disputes. The examples (10, 30, 60) are illustrative — the corpus does not enumerate accepted values. SOURCE: "Enter the amount, in days that will be the standard payment term of client to vendor (for example, 10, 30, or 60 days)." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/available-invoice-settings-8b3411f0.md

sequence.action: enter the NET discount terms if any
sequence.rationale: After the payment term and explicitly low-stakes: the corpus warns the value is informational only and feeds no calculation, so nothing downstream breaks if it is left at N/A. Ordering it here rather than earlier keeps a writer from mistaking it for a control that affects payment timing. SOURCE: "If a discount applies, enter the NET discount terms agreed upon with the supplier." plus the Note "The data in this field is for information purposes only. It is not used in any calculations." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/available-invoice-settings-8b3411f0.md

sequence.action: enter the percentage
sequence.rationale: Paired with order 2 and equally informational, but it carries the one hard data-type constraint on this page, which a writer must respect or the entry will not take: Number (11, 8). SOURCE: "Number (11, 8) - 11 characters maximum, 8 characters maximum to the right of the decimal." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/available-invoice-settings-8b3411f0.md

sequence.action: select the carrier code
sequence.rationale: Grouped with the other N/A-default supplier fields. Typed as a selection because the corpus verb is 'Select' and the value is a code — but the option list is nowhere enumerated in 2026_08, so a writer must be handed the code rather than choosing from documented values. SOURCE: "Select the preferred carrier for shipping. This is designated by a code representing the shipping method used by the supplier." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/available-invoice-settings-8b3411f0.md

sequence.action: set the shipping terms code
sequence.rationale: Immediately after the shipping method since they describe the same supplier arrangement. Flagging a genuine gap rather than papering over it: the corpus gives no verb for this control at all, so its widget type is undetermined and a writer must inspect it at runtime instead of assuming a text box or a list. SOURCE: "The code representing shipping terms with a supplier." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/available-invoice-settings-8b3411f0.md

sequence.action: enter the number of days before the billing date
sequence.rationale: Must be right before any recurring invoice is scheduled, not after — the offset is the lead time that lets a generated invoice clear approval workflow in time for the billing date, so a value set late means the first cycles are already too tight to approve. Defaults to 14 days. Title-casing of the label drifts between topics. SOURCE: "Enter the number of days you would like the invoice generated prior to the actual billing date in order for the system to generate the invoice in time for approval workflow and billing." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/available-invoice-settings-8b3411f0.md

sequence.action: select the additional fields to check alongside Vendor, then Save
sequence.field: Default fields that regulate duplicate invoices (Vendor is selected by default)
sequence.rationale: Sequenced BEFORE any work in the Audit Rules tool, and the corpus makes both halves of that dependency explicit: this page only chooses the basis, and the admin must then also create an Is Duplicate rule in Audit Rules — so a writer that stops here has configured detection that never runs. Two further constraints: Vendor is always checked and is not a selectable option, and using more than one field requires an AND statement when the rule is authored. Options are genuinely enumerated: Invoice Date, Invoice Amount, Invoice Number (default selection is Invoice Number). SOURCE: "On the Invoice Settings page, in the Default fields that regulate duplicate invoices (Vendor is selected by default) list, select the desired fields you want to use to check for duplicate invoices." and "After activating this feature, the admin must also create an Is Duplicate rule in the Audit Rules tool." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/fields-that-regulate-duplicate-invoices-b3b75abd.md

sequence.action: select the copy-down source
sequence.field: For purchase order-based invoices, from where should the Invoice Line allocation be copied?
sequence.rationale: Settle this before the PO policies from step g1-s2 start producing matched invoices, since it decides where every PO-based invoice line's allocation comes from and changing it later leaves two populations of differently-allocated invoices. That timing is inference; what the corpus fixes is the two options and the default. Both values are enumerated: 'From the associated purchase order line' (default) and 'From the copy-down configurations' — the latter also appears without the hyphen as 'From the copydown configurations', so tolerate both. SOURCE: "From the associated purchase order line option: to have PO allocations lines automatically copied down from the PO line to the associated invoice line." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/available-invoice-settings-8b3411f0.md

sequence.action: confirm or clear the check box
sequence.field: Allow Invoice users to delete images on payment requests created on their behalf
sequence.rationale: Grouped with the other permissive-by-default restrictions and reviewed together, because all three are Enabled (selected) out of the box — a writer scanning for empty boxes to tick will miss every one of them. Clearing this prevents users from removing images from invoices the AP User created and assigned to them. SOURCE: "Select to allow the Concur Invoice user to remove images attached to invoices created by the AP User and assigned to the user. Clear (disable) to prevent the user from removing images associated with the invoice." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/available-invoice-settings-8b3411f0.md

sequence.action: confirm or clear the check box
sequence.field: Allow processor users to change vendor on requests pending processor roles
sequence.rationale: Same permissive default as order 9 and reviewed alongside it. Note it interacts with the group-level owner permission in step g1-s3: vendor-change rights are governed in two places, so deciding only one leaves a gap. That interaction is inference from the two field descriptions, not a corpus statement. SOURCE: "Select to allow a Processor to change the vendor associated with an invoice even during workflow steps pending a Processor. Clear (disable) to prevent the Processor from changing the vendor if the invoice is pending any Processor role in workflow (accounting review)." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/available-invoice-settings-8b3411f0.md

sequence.action: clear the check box to restrict the role
sequence.field: Allow Payment Manager to change banking information
sequence.rationale: Inverted sense and the highest-risk misread on the page: the restrictive action is to CLEAR, and the default is Enabled (selected). One topic's prose contradicts itself by saying to 'select (enable) this setting to remove the Banking Import link' — its own numbered procedure and the settings table both say clear, so follow those and ignore the prose sentence. SOURCE: "Clear (disable) this check box to remove the Banking Import link from Payment Manager and prevent the Payment Manager role from importing any changes to banking information." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/available-invoice-settings-8b3411f0.md

sequence.action: select the check box if remittance emails are wanted
sequence.field: Send vendor payment email notifications for Check and ACH Concur Invoice Pay types
sequence.rationale: Late in the sequence because it is outbound-facing: enabling it sends vendors full remittance detail, so it should only be switched on once Invoice Pay Check/ACH is actually in use. Disabled (cleared) by default in Professional Edition; the covered payment types are enumerated as Check and ACH only. SOURCE: "Select (enable) this check box if you want vendors to receive an email when they are paid via ACH or Check with Invoice Pay. The email will contain full remittance information including when, how, and for what they are paid." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/available-invoice-settings-8b3411f0.md

sequence.action: select the check box
sequence.rationale: Last, and gated by two things outside this page — which is exactly why it cannot be attempted earlier. SAP Concur staff must enable the feature via a service request first, and this box only unlocks it: the real configuration happens on the separate Peppol Configuration page under Invoice Processing Admin, whose own Peppol Integration Enablement field is a distinct Active/Inactive selector. Disabled (cleared) by default. SOURCE: "Select (enable) this check box to allow Peppol Integration and configure the feature in Concur Invoice." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/available-invoice-settings-8b3411f0.md; prerequisite "The Peppol Integration feature for Concur Invoice must be enabled by SAP Concur staff. Clients must initiate a service request with SAP Concur support." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/feature-activation-04b47637.md
